## Goals

1. Access a virtualized computing environment as a local Docker container.
2. Integrate your computing environment with VS Code.
3. Configure Git for documenting your work and submitting assignments.
4. Practice setting up software in a Unix-like environment.

## The Tools

You are responsible for installing the following on your machine:

1. [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
2. [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/download)

Once you create a container using the class image, you will have access to:

1. a [Unix Shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_shell) (we will use `zsh` by default),
2. [Git](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Git),
3. [Quarto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarto_(software)), and
4. [Julia 1.12.7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_(programming_language)).

In addition to various tools installed on the image (i.e. Unix utilities), you also have access to

1. [Python 3.14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language)),
2. [R 4.5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R_(programming_language)), and
3. [DuckDB 1.5.5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DuckDB).

## On Your Own

### 1. Get the class Docker image working on your computer

Read the guide on [how to use Docker](/howto/use_docker.qmd) in this class.

### 2. Practice using the terminal

Read the notes on [the Unix shell](/notes/module01/unix.qmd) and experiment inside a container.

### 3. Read up on Git, GitHub, the SSH protocol

Try setting up Git on your container and create your GitHub account.

1. [What is Git?](../notes/module01/git.qmd) and [How to configure Git](../howto/configure_git.qmd).
2. [How to set up your GitHub account](../howto/setup_github.qmd).
3. [What is SSH?](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/connecting-to-github-with-ssh/about-ssh).


## In Person

The following tasks involve using the class Docker image.
Instructions are to be carried out inside a running container unless otherwise specified.

### 1. Download and install Quarto

1. Inside your terminal, run `uname -m` to determine whether your container is setup with an `arm64` or `x86_64` architecture.

2. Based on the result in the previous step, download Quarto using `curl`:

    ```default
    curl -fL -o quarto.tar.gz \
    https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/download/v1.10.18/quarto-1.10.18-linux-arm64.tar.gz
    ```

    or

    ```default
    curl -fL -o quarto.tar.gz \
    https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/download/v1.10.18/quarto-1.10.18-linux-amd64.tar.gz
    ```

3. Next, unpack files from the tarball into `/home/student/.local`:

    ```default
    tar -xvzf quarto.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C ~/.local
    ```

4. Finally, check that Quarto can be run from your terminal (and therefore seen by other programs) with

    ```default
    quarto check
    ```

### 2. Let us know your GitHub username

Fill out the [Google form](https://forms.gle/NjciYpV6sePL2ZvL9) to record the username you wish to use for this course. It will be used to set up your private repository for this class.

### 3. Fill out the class survey

See [this Google form](https://forms.gle/am7qCGiuBuk4CTuBA) to answer a few questions. It will help the instructors understand everyone's background.

### 4. Practice creating your first Quarto document

See the notes on [Quarto](../notes/module01/quarto.qmd) and explore Quarto's features.
